subject: dsa
title: Linked List Cycle
summary: Run two pointers: slow moves one node per step, fast moves two. If the list loops, fast keeps lapping the loop and eventually lands on slow.
problem: Return true if the linked list has a cycle: some node's next pointer revisits an earlier node.

steps.caption: Does this list cycle? Node -4's arrow loops back to 2, so following next never ends. Detect it with two runners moving at different speeds.
Start both at the head. Each step, slow moves 1 node and fast moves 2. If fast meets slow there's a cycle; if fast runs off the end, there isn't.
Step 1: slow advances to 2, fast takes two hops to 0.
Step 2: slow moves to 0; fast takes two hops through the loop and lands back on 2.
Step 3: slow moves to -4, and fast's two hops land on -4 as well. They meet on the same node!
Fast caught slow inside the loop, so the list has a cycle: return true. With no cycle, fast would have reached null first.
